project.name: omi-memory-ingestion-pipeline

Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: users.py
nodes.summary: Provides the Firestore-backed user-data repository for platform metadata, account-deletion workflow state, payment details, language preferences, and subscriptions. It also contains the transactional claim and recovery guards that keep destructive deletion work durable and single-owner.

nodes.name: DeletionWipeTaskResolution
nodes.summary: Typed dictionary contract describing how a deletion task lookup resolved and, when actionable, which user it belongs to.

nodes.name: DeletionWipeIntent
nodes.summary: Typed dictionary returned when a deletion request creates or joins the durable wipe authority, including the opaque job ID and dispatch ownership.

nodes.name: _normalize_platform
nodes.summary: Maps a raw application-platform value to a coarse desktop, mobile, or web bucket and preserves the normalized operating-system value.

nodes.name: record_client_device
nodes.summary: Upserts a user client-device projection with platform, device class, version, labels, and first/last-seen timestamps behind a Redis write lock.

nodes.name: record_user_platform
nodes.summary: Throttles and records coarse and detailed platform activity on the user document, setting signup metadata once and accumulating platforms used.

nodes.name: is_exists_user
nodes.summary: Checks whether the canonical Firestore user document exists for a UID.

nodes.name: get_user_profile
nodes.summary: Reads and returns the full Firestore user profile, using an empty mapping when the document is absent.

nodes.name: get_user_time_zone
nodes.summary: Reads retained account timezone metadata and returns only a non-empty string value.

nodes.name: set_user_cancellation_feedback
nodes.summary: Persists a user's cancellation reason, optional detail, and timestamp into the profile projection.

nodes.name: mark_user_deletion_wipe_running
nodes.summary: Marks a queued deletion worker as running so reconciliation distinguishes active work from an abandoned pending marker.

nodes.name: _deletion_wipe_needs_dispatch
nodes.summary: Determines whether a deletion record is failed or stale enough to permit another dispatch attempt.

nodes.name: _mark_user_deletion_wipe_intent_txn
nodes.summary: Transactionally creates or joins a deletion-wipe intent while preserving an existing job identity and refusing to rewind active or completed work.

nodes.name: mark_user_deletion_wipe_intent
nodes.summary: Creates a candidate opaque deletion job ID and delegates durable intent creation to the Firestore transaction guard.

nodes.name: _mark_user_deletion_wipe_started_txn
nodes.summary: Atomically fences one deletion dispatch attempt and transitions an eligible intent to pending with its dispatch identity.

nodes.name: mark_user_deletion_wipe_started
nodes.summary: Runs the transaction that reserves a newly created or retryable deletion dispatch attempt.

nodes.name: _mark_deletion_wipe_dispatched_txn
nodes.summary: Records a queue handoff timestamp only for the matching job and dispatch ID, without moving worker state backward.

nodes.name: mark_deletion_wipe_dispatched
nodes.summary: Uses the selected Firestore client to persist confirmed deletion-task dispatch under the job authority.

nodes.name: require_deletion_wipe_dispatch
nodes.summary: Verifies that a deletion intent has either reached a worker or has a confirmed queue handoff before the request is accepted.

nodes.name: _mark_deletion_wipe_dispatch_failed_txn
nodes.summary: Transactionally records a fenced dispatch failure only when the job and dispatch attempt still match and no worker has progressed.

nodes.name: mark_deletion_wipe_dispatch_failed
nodes.summary: Persists a dispatch failure through the chosen Firestore client without reopening an executing wipe.

nodes.name: mark_user_deletion_wipe_completed
nodes.summary: Marks the durable account-deletion data wipe completed with its completion timestamp.

nodes.name: mark_user_deletion_wipe_failed
nodes.summary: Marks a failed background wipe so reconciliation can retry it instead of treating partial cleanup as success.

nodes.name: _ensure_deletion_wipe_job_id_txn
nodes.summary: Backfills a missing opaque job ID in an existing deletion record without replacing an established identity.

nodes.name: ensure_deletion_wipe_job_id
nodes.summary: Provides transactional job-identity recovery for deletion records created before job IDs were stored.

nodes.name: resolve_deletion_wipe_job_id
nodes.summary: Resolves an opaque deletion task ID to one canonical account-deletion record and classifies missing, ambiguous, terminal, or actionable states.

nodes.name: resolve_legacy_deletion_wipe_uid
nodes.summary: Converts a legacy UID task payload into a still-actionable canonical deletion record while refusing completed or non-actionable states.

nodes.name: _mark_user_deletion_billing_failed_txn
nodes.summary: Transactionally records provider-cancellation failure while preserving any actionable or terminal deletion state.

nodes.name: mark_user_deletion_billing_failed
nodes.summary: Records that billing cancellation blocked deletion before destructive cleanup could begin.

nodes.name: cancel_user_deletion_wipe
nodes.summary: Cancels a persisted wipe marker when authentication deletion fails, preventing later reconciliation from deleting a live account.

nodes.name: get_pending_deletion_wipes
nodes.summary: Collects failed and stale deletion markers across pending, running, deleting-auth, and retrying states for bounded reconciliation, applying age checks in Python to avoid composite indexes.

nodes.name: _claim_deletion_wipe_txn
nodes.summary: Transactionally claims only failed or sufficiently stale deletion records for re-enqueueing, fencing fresh workers and concurrent reconciler runs.

nodes.name: claim_deletion_wipe
nodes.summary: Attempts to acquire the durable re-enqueue claim for one deletion record and returns the UID only when ownership is won.

nodes.name: _claim_deletion_wipe_task_txn
nodes.summary: Claims a Cloud Tasks delivery, preserving retrying state until the worker starts and recognizing completed, running, missing, and non-actionable records.

nodes.name: claim_deletion_wipe_for_task
nodes.summary: Exposes the transactional Cloud Tasks delivery claim and its bounded deletion-state outcomes.

nodes.name: delete_user_data
nodes.summary: Recursively deletes all retained user subcollections and the root user document, including children that outlive a missing parent document.

nodes.name: set_paypal_payment_details
nodes.summary: Updates the stored PayPal payment projection for a user.

nodes.name: get_paypal_payment_details
nodes.summary: Reads the user's stored PayPal payment projection when present.

nodes.name: set_default_payment_method
nodes.summary: Stores the user's default payment-method identifier in the profile document.

nodes.name: get_default_payment_method
nodes.summary: Reads the user's default payment-method identifier from Firestore.

nodes.name: get_user_language_preference
nodes.summary: Reads a typed language projection through the bounded cache policy, falling back to a Firestore field read when needed.

nodes.name: set_user_language_preference
nodes.summary: Persists a user's language preference and invalidates the matching low-risk cache entry.

nodes.name: get_user_subscription
nodes.summary: Reads and strictly parses a stored subscription, creating and persisting the default free subscription when no subscription exists.

nodes.name: get_existing_user_subscription
nodes.summary: Reads and strictly parses only an existing stored subscription without creating a default record.

nodes.name: get_user_valid_subscription
nodes.summary: Returns an active free entitlement or currently valid paid subscription, falling back to the default free plan when paid entitlement is no longer current.

nodes.name: account_deletion.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates durable account deletion from intent persistence through billing cancellation, Firebase Auth removal, Firestore cleanup, Cloud Tasks dispatch, failure marking, telemetry, and reconciliation. The service keeps irreversible work behind durable state and worker claims so queue failures remain recoverable.

nodes.name: AccountCleanupFailure
nodes.summary: Wraps a cleanup exception with the named irreversible operation that failed, allowing the worker to emit bounded failure telemetry and retry state.

nodes.name: _emit_deletion_telemetry
nodes.summary: Emits account-deletion completion or failure telemetry with UID-bearing properties removed and person-profile processing disabled.

nodes.name: _perform_account_cleanup
nodes.summary: Runs the required cleanup sequence: cancel billing, delete Firebase Auth, and recursively wipe authoritative Firestore user data, preserving the failed operation in an AccountCleanupFailure.

nodes.name: background_wipe_user_data
nodes.summary: Executes a claimed deletion wipe, marks running/completed/failed durable state, and emits bounded terminal telemetry while preserving retryability after partial failure.

nodes.name: enqueue_deletion_wipe
nodes.summary: Dispatches a deletion job through configured Cloud Tasks or the explicitly retained inline local/dev/test executor path.

nodes.name: _mark_wipe_failed_after_enqueue_error
nodes.summary: Best-effort persists a fenced dispatch failure after queue submission errors and sanitizes the diagnostic context if that persistence also fails.

nodes.name: _retry_firestore_write
nodes.summary: Retries a Firestore write with bounded backoff and either raises a sanitized failure or logs it according to the caller's policy.

nodes.name: _cancel_subscription_for_account_deletion
nodes.summary: Loads a user's subscription, confirms provider cancellation when a billing ID exists, and records a billing-blocked deletion state on failure.

nodes.name: start_account_deletion
nodes.summary: Persists an actionable deletion intent, reserves a dispatch attempt, enqueues the wipe, and accepts the request only after queue handoff or worker execution is durably proven.

nodes.name: _is_auth_user_gone
nodes.summary: Checks whether Firebase Auth definitively reports a missing user and fails safe on every other or indeterminate error.

nodes.name: reconcile_pending_deletion_wipes
nodes.summary: Finds stale or failed deletion records, verifies stale deleting-auth records, claims each job transactionally, restores missing job IDs, and re-enqueues recoverable work without duplicate ownership.

nodes.name: AppState.swift

It also centralizes system notification names used by desktop navigation, capture recovery, Rewind, tasks, and chat surfaces.
nodes.languageNotes: SwiftUI ObservableObject state is isolated to MainActor while asynchronous lifecycle callbacks re-enter it explicitly; related local-profile and product-identity behavior is supplied by OmiSupport imports.

nodes.name: FinishConversationResult

nodes.name: AppState

nodes.name: extension Notification.Name
nodes.summary: Declares the shared notification vocabulary for lifecycle, capture permissions, Home/Chat navigation, Rewind, tasks, insights, refresh, conversation deletion, automation, and transcription toggles.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Maps concrete system-audio capture errors to denied, unknown, unsupported, or granted-independent permission status, preserving uncertainty for non-permission failures.

nodes.name: quiesceCurrentAmbientCaptureForOwnerTransition
nodes.summary: Provides a static transition hook that asks the current AppState to quiesce ambient capture before an owner change.

nodes.name: resetOwnerScopedContent
nodes.summary: Invalidates in-flight owner-scoped work and clears folders, filters, counts, errors, loading flags, and live speaker names after an in-place account switch.

nodes.name: AppState.init
nodes.summary: Registers the current AppState, wires owner and conversation callbacks, resets stale paywall cache state, prepares backend routing, loads environment, installs lifecycle observers, and initializes permission/health checks.

nodes.name: setupLifecycleObservers
nodes.summary: Installs observers for termination, sleep/wake, screen lock/unlock, system-audio mode changes, and CoreAudio recovery, finalizing or restarting local transcription as appropriate.

nodes.name: AppState.deinit
nodes.summary: Removes lifecycle and owner-change observers when the application state coordinator is released.

nodes.name: billing.json

nodes.name: qualification.json

nodes.name: understand-anything.json

nodes.name: account-lifecycle.json

nodes.name: capture-transcription.json

nodes.name: LocalTranscriptFormatter

nodes.name: LocalTranscriptFormatter.normalize
nodes.summary: Merges incoming transcript segments into the retained local projection, removes replaced tails, cleans text, and assigns contiguous segment order values.

nodes.name: LocalTranscriptFormatter.format
nodes.summary: Renders normalized segments with resolved speaker labels and optional timestamps only when every segment timeline is safe to display.

nodes.name: LocalTranscriptFormatter.canDisplayTimestamps
nodes.summary: Rejects timestamp rendering when any pair of segments overlaps or is chronologically inconsistent.

nodes.name: LocalTranscriptFormatter.stableSegmentId
nodes.summary: Keeps a valid provider UUID or derives a deterministic UUIDv5-shaped identifier from the conversation and segment input using SHA-256.

nodes.name: LocalTranscriptFormatter.merge
nodes.summary: Combines adjacent same-speaker or incomplete cross-speaker text while preserving sentence boundaries, translations, and timing.

nodes.name: LocalTranscriptFormatter.sentencePieces
nodes.summary: Splits trimmed transcript text at the formatter's multilingual sentence-ending characters and preserves a final unterminated tail.

nodes.name: LocalTranscriptFormatter.chronologicallyOrdered
nodes.summary: Orders segments by spoken start time, then original source order and array position to make equal-time ordering deterministic.

nodes.name: TranscriptionStorage+LocalAuthority.swift
nodes.summary: Implements the owner-local transcription authority: conversation capture, segment and translation persistence, folders and labels, search and detail reads, enrichment work, recovery, discard handling, and terminal lifecycle admission in GRDB.

nodes.name: beginConversation
nodes.summary: Creates a locally authoritative recording session after validating the conversation UUID, writing capture configuration, and establishing the first durable session row under a commit lease.

nodes.name: upsertSegments
nodes.summary: Validates the recording session, upserts nonblank incoming segments with stable IDs and translations, rebuilds normalized transcript rows, and advances content generation.

nodes.name: attachTranslation
nodes.summary: Validates and attaches a translation to an ingested segment, then reuses the session-based segment upsert path so local transcript state stays consistent.

nodes.name: conversationDetail
nodes.summary: Reads one local conversation and assembles its persisted metadata, speaker labels, and ordered transcript segments.

nodes.name: setConversationLocation
nodes.summary: Writes a location snapshot only for a still-recording conversation that has no location, guarded by authorization and a commit lease.

nodes.name: conversationPage
nodes.summary: Queries bounded local conversation pages using lifecycle, star, date, and folder filters and maps rows into local summaries.

nodes.name: conversationCount
nodes.summary: Counts local conversations using the same owner-local lifecycle and filter predicate as paged reads.

nodes.name: fairUseEvidence
nodes.summary: Builds bounded, content-trimmed fair-use evidence for recent non-recording conversations without making the evidence a product-data authority.

nodes.name: searchConversations
nodes.summary: Normalizes and escapes user search text, then searches local titles and overviews while excluding active recording and merge sessions.

nodes.name: setConversationStarred
nodes.summary: Updates a conversation's local starred flag under authorization and returns the refreshed local detail.

nodes.name: setConversationTitle
nodes.summary: Validates a local title, fences the write by conversation generation and lifecycle state, and schedules the resulting enrichment work.

nodes.name: applyConversationStructureCandidate
nodes.summary: Commits bounded remote structure candidates only when the captured owner and content generation remain current, updating title, overview, emoji, and commitments locally.

nodes.name: conversationFolders
nodes.summary: Lists owner-local conversation folders in stable name order.

nodes.name: createConversationFolder
nodes.summary: Validates and inserts a local conversation folder while rejecting duplicate names.

nodes.name: updateConversationFolder
nodes.summary: Validates a folder rename and updates its local timestamp while preserving folder identity.

nodes.name: moveConversation
nodes.summary: Moves a local conversation to a selected folder or clears its folder assignment after validating both records.

nodes.name: deleteConversationFolder
nodes.summary: Deletes a folder only after confirming it is not referenced by conversations, preserving local referential safety.

nodes.name: setConversationSpeakerLabel
nodes.summary: Validates and upserts a speaker label for a local conversation, then returns the refreshed conversation detail.

nodes.name: deleteConversationCascade
nodes.summary: Deletes a conversation and its dependent local capture, transcript, label, folder, and enrichment rows as one authorized cascade.

nodes.name: mergeConversations
nodes.summary: Merges source conversations into a destination while preserving ordered segments, labels, metadata, and generation fencing under one local commit.

nodes.name: finishConversation
nodes.summary: Transitions a recording session into local finalization, writes terminal timing and reason data, and admits bounded enrichment work.

nodes.name: recoverLocalFinalization
nodes.summary: Recovers sessions left in transient finalization states after launch, reporting repaired, skipped, and failed local sessions.

nodes.name: enrichmentWork
nodes.summary: Lists enrichment work for a conversation and exposes its local state, attempt count, errors, and generation.

nodes.name: retryConversationEnrichment
nodes.summary: Reopens eligible failed or stale enrichment work for a current conversation generation with bounded retry fencing.

nodes.name: recoverAndListPendingEnrichmentWork
nodes.summary: Recovers running work left by an interrupted process and returns pending enrichment work eligible for a worker to claim.

nodes.name: claimDiscardWork
nodes.summary: Claims one discard job using generation and attempt fencing so only the current worker can resolve destructive local work.

nodes.name: claimEnrichmentWork
nodes.summary: Claims one structure or action-item enrichment job with state, generation, and attempt checks.

nodes.name: completeStructureWork
nodes.summary: Validates a structure candidate against the current generation, applies its bounded fields, and marks structure enrichment terminal atomically.

nodes.name: relatedOpenActionItems
nodes.summary: Loads open local action items related to a conversation for candidate reconciliation.

nodes.name: conversationActionItems
nodes.summary: Loads local action items linked to a conversation, including completion, deletion, due-date, and provenance fields.

nodes.name: completeActionItemsWork
nodes.summary: Applies create, update, and complete action-item candidates with token fencing and rolls the conversation to completion when enrichment is terminal.

nodes.name: failEnrichmentWork
nodes.summary: Records a fenced enrichment failure, retaining retryable work below the attempt limit and completing the conversation when no work remains.

nodes.name: resolveDiscardWork
nodes.summary: Resolves a discard candidate against the current generation, either deleting the conversation or re-admitting structure and action-item work.

nodes.name: failDiscardWorkKeepingConversation
nodes.summary: Records a discard failure while keeping the conversation, re-admitting non-destructive enrichment work for recovery.

nodes.name: localAuthorityAuthorization
nodes.summary: Builds or validates the local mutation authorization snapshot, allowing injected test databases while rejecting revoked runtime ownership.

nodes.name: fetchLocalSegments
nodes.summary: Reads ordered local transcript rows and decodes their persisted translations into transcript segments.

nodes.name: makeLocalConversationDetail
nodes.summary: Maps a database row and related labels and segments into the owner-local conversation detail model.

nodes.name: makeLocalConversationSummary
nodes.summary: Maps one database row into the compact local conversation summary model used by list and search projections.

nodes.name: localConversationPredicate
nodes.summary: Builds the SQL predicate and bound arguments for local lifecycle, star, date, and folder filters.

nodes.name: admitWork
nodes.summary: Inserts pending enrichment work idempotently for a conversation generation and kind.

nodes.name: completeConversationWhenEnrichmentIsTerminal
nodes.summary: Marks a conversation completed only after structure and action-item work for its generation leave pending and running states.

nodes.name: supersedeDiscardAndReadmit
nodes.summary: Supersedes stale discard work and admits a replacement discard job for the current content generation.

nodes.name: extension TranscriptionStorage
nodes.summary: Defines the TranscriptionStorage extension that owns local conversation persistence, mutation authorization, enrichment work, recovery, and terminal lifecycle transitions.

nodes.name: upsertSegments
nodes.summary: Resolves a session ID to its conversation ID under authorization and delegates to the canonical conversation-based segment upsert path.

nodes.name: overview.json
nodes.summary: OpenWiki architecture claim ledger recording evidence-backed statements about router composition, memory ownership versus backend compute, and the managed Pi adapter alongside local conversation journaling.
nodes.languageNotes: JSON configuration with schema, page-version, claim, and verification sections.

nodes.name: development.json
nodes.summary: OpenWiki claim manifest for development operations, capturing repository setup, pinned runtimes, dependency synchronization, launcher and CI checks, UA preparation, and PR closeout contracts.

nodes.name: migrations.json
nodes.summary: OpenWiki claim manifest describing retained migration operations: named GRDB migrations for Rewind schema evolution and a credentialed, resumable Mixpanel export protected by a concurrency lock.

nodes.name: quickstart.json
nodes.summary: Stores verified OpenWiki claims about the repository's canonical FastAPI backend, desktop and transient compute routes, Node agent build and test surface, and setup checks. Each claim carries source evidence and a verification record.

nodes.name: .last-update.json
nodes.summary: Records the most recent OpenWiki update metadata, including timestamp, command, Git head, model, completion status, and output language.

nodes.name: .page-manifest.json
nodes.summary: Maps generated OpenWiki page paths to source fingerprints, page versions, Git heads, completion authors, and run identifiers so documentation freshness can be tracked.

layers.name: Backend API & Orchestration
layers.description: FastAPI startup, authenticated routers, live-listen session entrypoints, and backend response templates expose Intentive capabilities to clients.

layers.name: Backend Services, Providers & Policies
layers.description: Backend services, speech and LLM integrations, billing, retrieval, observability, admission policies, and shared operational utilities implement application behavior.

layers.name: Backend Persistence & Data Models
layers.description: Firestore and Redis adapters, transactional persistence, caches, and Pydantic models define the backend data boundary and durable state shape.

layers.name: macOS Product Interface
layers.description: SwiftUI windows, pages, settings, chat surfaces, floating controls, onboarding, Rewind presentation, and visual tokens form the native macOS product interface.

layers.name: macOS Capture, Runtime & Local Data
layers.description: Native runtime services own audio and screen capture, transcription, application state, authentication, local stores, Rewind processing, automation, and provider-facing behavior.

layers.name: Node Agent Runtime
layers.description: The bundled TypeScript agent and Pi extension implement the local model/tool loop, RPC protocol, runtime contracts, adapters, and journal-facing agent support.

layers.name: Build, Deployment & Repository Configuration
layers.description: Container definitions, release and runtime matrices, package and tool configuration, native build helpers, emulator rules, and local test or launch scripts shape delivery.

layers.name: Documentation & Evidence
layers.description: OpenWiki claims, manifests, agent metadata, update records, and bundled legal documentation preserve the repository’s verified architecture and operating context.

tour.title: Backend Application Entry Point
tour.description: Start with the FastAPI application entry point, which loads backend configuration, registers routers, initializes shared services, and reconciles pending account-deletion work during startup and shutdown. Its imports provide the clearest high-level map of the Python side before the tour moves into individual boundaries.

tour.title: Authenticated API Surface
tour.description: Building on the router registration from Step 1, these endpoints expose the authenticated desktop, realtime, conversation-compute, and memory-compute boundaries. They show how request handling stays at the API edge while deeper services and local clients remain separate responsibilities.

tour.title: Live Listening and Transcripts
tour.description: The listening route separates socket admission, receiving, transient persistence, and transcript projection rather than treating live speech as a stored conversation. Read these files together to see how streaming STT, segment contracts, and backend-side chronology form one bounded request path.

tour.title: Services and Recovery Policies
tour.description: These service modules implement provider, billing, task-dispatch, and executor policies behind the API routes. The account-deletion service is the key recovery example: irreversible work is staged behind durable state, worker claims, failure marking, and reconciliation so a queue or provider failure remains recoverable.

tour.title: Persistence and Account Data
tour.description: The persistence layer holds the Firestore, Redis, and domain-model boundaries used by the services and routers above. In particular, `users.py` owns account metadata and the transactional deletion-wipe guards, while the user model and data-export service keep the repository vocabulary explicit.

tour.title: macOS State and Product Shell
tour.description: The macOS application shell turns backend capabilities into local product state and visible surfaces. `AppState.swift` is the central main-actor owner for transcription, conversations, permissions, lifecycle notifications, and scoped UI reset, while the home/chat files show how that state reaches the user-facing shell.

tour.title: Local Transcript and Rewind Authority
tour.description: After seeing live segments enter the app, follow their owner-local persistence and read paths here. The formatter applies chronology, normalization, stable IDs, and timestamp safety, while the local-authority and database extensions own GRDB writes, recovery, translations, search, and lifecycle admission.

tour.title: Bundled Node Agent Runtime
tour.description: The bundled Node process is the agent runtime behind the macOS bridge: it speaks a JSONL protocol, coordinates the kernel loop, routes desktop intents, and applies tool policy. These files show the boundary between the Swift host and the managed agent without conflating the agent runtime with the backend API layer.

tour.title: Capture Voice and Assistant Runtime
tour.description: The capture and voice modules explain how audio, ambient assistance, transcription, and realtime turn state are coordinated on macOS. They are adjacent but distinct runtime responsibilities, which makes this a useful stop for understanding where capture ends and transcript, chat, or voice-turn handling begins.

tour.title: User-Facing Workspaces
tour.description: These pages and compute clients show how conversations, memories, and settings are presented as local product workspaces while remote calls remain narrow compute contracts. They build on the state owner and local storage boundaries from Steps 6 and 7 rather than creating a second persistence authority.

tour.title: Build and Runtime Configuration
tour.description: The repository-level configuration defines how the backend, desktop bundle, and agent are built and run together. The container definition, runtime environment, route policy, macOS bundle metadata, and package manifest make deployment and local execution boundaries visible without turning configuration into application logic.
tour.languageLesson: Container and YAML configuration are declarative: the files describe desired build, routing, and runtime state, while the application modules remain responsible for behavior and validation.

tour.title: Documentation and Evidence Contracts
tour.description: Finish with the repository’s documentation and evidence artifacts, which record how architecture, workflows, release operations, and graph freshness are checked against source. The Understand Anything claim manifest is included because it documents the owned Luna/system-fork refresh contract and its stop conditions alongside the broader architecture evidence.

components.name: Screen capture
components.summary: The macOS ProactiveAssistantsPlugin owns monitoring admission, permission/privacy/idle/context gates, capture cadence and owner fencing. A permitted frame is distributed to live assistants and local Rewind; excluded applications are blocked from both paths. Permission failures retry with bounded backoff, while engine failures pause and recover or stop with a user-visible failure.

components.name: Rewind
components.summary: RewindIndexer turns accepted captured frames into owner-scoped local video chunks and screenshot metadata. It deduplicates frames, samples and deduplicates OCR, queues optional remote OCR embedding, and publishes local updates. RewindDatabase supplies local FTS and retention/rebuild operations; RewindViewModel combines local FTS with local vector similarity for UI and ChatToolExecutor can consume that retrieval.

components.name: Ambient transcription
components.summary: AppState admits a local conversation before capture, then selects two on-device Parakeet producers on supported Apple Silicon or an authenticated Python /v4/listen WebSocket path for managed STT. Microphone and system audio remain separate in local mode for speaker attribution; managed mode mixes audio. Segment callbacks preserve stable IDs, corrections, spoken-time ordering and translations before durable local SQLite upserts. Local model failure and managed reconnect/fair-use exhaustion have bounded handoffs, and finishing drains producers before closing the local conversation.

components.name: Conversation enrichment
components.summary: ConversationFinalizationService closes local sessions, admits or discards them, and runs structure and action-item enrichment with recovery. Each enrichment claims local work for a content generation and attempt, sends bounded transcript candidates to authenticated stateless compute, validates generation-scoped responses, then commits only under current owner authorization; failures remain retryable up to the local policy. The local store remains authoritative.

components.name: Monitoring admission
components.summary: Checks paywall, permission, notification and startup races before monitoring; bounded retries revisit permission without prompting on non-user paths.

components.name: Active-window capture engine
components.summary: Resolves the active window and captures through ScreenCaptureKit or the supported fallback while enforcing recording permission and capture capability.

components.name: Gated frame distribution
components.summary: Applies privacy, idle, context and owner checks, then sends one accepted frame to live assistants and Rewind with recovery around transient failures. Rewind separately drops frames while its encoder is busy; assistant tasks have their own per-assistant backpressure.

components.name: Frame deduplication and owner fencing
components.summary: Rejects stale owner work and repeated app/window/hash frames while retaining capture anchors for the dedupe interval.

components.name: Video and selected OCR indexer
components.summary: Encodes accepted frames into local chunks, runs throttled/deduplicated OCR, records metadata, and asynchronously queues OCR embeddings.

components.name: Rewind records and retention
components.summary: Stores screenshot metadata and video references, performs local FTS/search and retention cleanup, and supports transactional chunk rebuild.

components.name: Rewind local retrieval
components.summary: Combines local FTS and local embedding similarity for timeline/search presentation and exposes selected results to chat tools. Semantic queries call remote embedContent, then score owner-local embedding blobs locally; raw OCR/vector records are not a hosted search authority.

components.name: Local mic and system audio producers
components.summary: Starts separate user-mic and other-speaker local transcription services and reconciles microphone/system capture policy with meeting and platform availability.

components.name: Managed listen client
components.summary: Streams mixed signed PCM to the authenticated listen WebSocket and reports transcript, status, reconnect and fair-use events.

components.name: Segment correction and ordering
components.summary: Upserts stable segment IDs, preserves translations and tie arrival order, and projects spoken-time ordering to the live transcript.

components.name: Local conversation persistence
components.summary: Owns local conversation/session identity, segment upserts, generation and finalization state used by capture and enrichment.

components.name: Finalization coordinator and recovery
components.summary: Closes local sessions, schedules admission/enrichment, recovers abandoned recordings at launch and retries pending durable work.

components.name: Conversation discard admission
components.summary: Runs durable discard admission before enrichment and keeps local work on classifier failure according to the admission policy.

components.name: Conversation structure enrichment
components.summary: Claims generation-scoped structure work, requests bounded candidates, validates them, preserves manual titles and commits locally.

components.name: Conversation action-item enrichment
components.summary: Matches bounded model action candidates against tokenized local open tasks and applies authorized create/update/complete mutations.

components.name: Generation, owner and retry guards
components.summary: Rejects stale owner/generation/attempt results and records retryable failures while preserving local authority.

components.name: Background assistants
components.summary: Owner-bound macOS orchestration for Focus, Insights, Memory, Tasks and Suggestions. It gates captured frames locally, applies cadence and backpressure, uses transient model analysis where needed, and routes accepted outcomes to local authorities or notifications.

components.name: Assistant scheduler
components.summary: Registers assistants and distributes owner-authorized frames. Each assistant gets one authorization slot; stale owners, disabled assistants and duplicate work are rejected, while reset and stop cancel pending work.

components.name: Focus assistant
components.summary: Analyzes supplied screenshots against local profile, goals, tasks and memories, persists only authorized focus status transitions, and exposes a bounded local projection with owner reset and notification feedback.

components.name: Insights assistant
components.summary: Builds local activity context and prior tips, asks transient image/tool analysis for bounded advice, then stores accepted advice as tagged interesting Memory rows. InsightStorage reads and mutates those rows rather than owning a second database. A bounded text/tool investigation precedes a screenshot/tool advice phase; provider tool calls are executed and interpreted locally before accepted advice is stored.

components.name: Memory extraction assistant
components.summary: Consumes owner-authorized captured frames after exclusion, cadence, settings and confidence gates. Screen analysis is blocked unless both assistant settings and notifications are enabled; accepted candidates are persisted locally as screenshot provenance and do not enter the lifecycle worker as conversation extraction.

components.name: Suggestion assistant
components.summary: Grounds a settled screen context in local tasks, memories and Rewind history, then applies ownership, duplicate, cooldown, settings and daily-budget gates around a transient suggestion before notification delivery.

components.name: Memory
components.summary: Owner-local GRDB authority for Memory assertions, Short-term/Long-term/Archive layers, expiry, dismissal, deletion/Undo, provenance and local reads. It admits bounded candidates and records durable processing work; remote services never become the Memory store.

components.name: Memory acceptance and lifecycle
components.summary: Trims assertions, assigns 30-day Short-term expiry, creates provenance and durable normalize/embed/consolidate work, and commits proposals only when work lease, owner generation and input revision still match. Extraction admissions are bounded, unique and idempotent.

components.name: Local semantic memory retrieval
components.summary: Authorized local Memory recall embeds the query through managed compute, reads revision-matched local vectors, filters pending-delete/dismissed/expired rows, checks dimensions and ranks cosine matches locally. Background assistants separately use local list/literal reads.

components.name: Tasks
components.summary: Owner-local action items provide creation, querying, completion, recurrence, editing, reorder, deletion/restore, provenance and reminders; transient assistant or conversation candidates cannot bypass this authority.

components.name: Task assistant
components.summary: Classifies screenshot context into task candidates, grounds against local FTS/vector tasks, rejects duplicates and non-deliverable candidates, then inserts accepted records with screenshot and provenance evidence.

components.name: Action item persistence
components.summary: ActionItemStorage owns active/completed/deleted reads, FTS, insert-if-active-description-absent deduplication, observations, recurrence and local embeddings.

components.name: Tasks projection and reminders
components.summary: TasksStore reads the local authority first, applies owner-generation fences, manages five-second undo/purge and projects reminders from authoritative open tasks; reminder failures do not roll back committed tasks.

components.name: Notifications
components.summary: NotificationService applies owner, settings, frequency and authorization gates for proactive results, while floating-bar presentation provides the owner-bound local chat continuation and native banners remain functional notices.

components.name: Notification policy and delivery
components.summary: Applies owner, settings and frequency policy before routing proactive outcomes to the floating bar or functional native delivery, and drops stale owner metadata on reset.

components.name: Native system banner delivery
components.summary: Optional functional notices delivered through UNUserNotificationCenter; this path does not provide the floating-card click-to-Chat continuation.

components.name: Floating notification cards and response actions
components.summary: Queues cards behind active chat/card state, auto-dismisses after a short presentation window, and on current-card click admits an owner-bound proactive journal receipt before opening local chat; dismiss and timeout only advance presentation.

components.name: Chat
components.summary: ChatProvider coordinates a typed turn, selected kernel context, local journal admission, streamed model/tool projections, and visible answer completion through the local agent runtime.

components.name: Realtime voice
components.summary: RealtimeHubSession owns the direct Gemini Live WebSocket lane with ephemeral-token minting, PCM input/output, transcription, owner and turn admission, bounded tool continuation, reconnect, and batch STT-to-Chat-to-TTS recovery.

components.name: Managed inference
components.summary: Authenticated remote compute services for native Chat streaming, background Gemini generation and embeddings, bounded Memory/conversation candidates, managed transcription, Live token minting and spoken-output fallback. Routes have distinct admission/transport behavior; product records remain local.

components.name: Authorized tools
components.summary: ChatToolExecutor validates owner and capability state, dispatches generated tools for local retrieval, SQL, tasks, memories, conversations, capture, and permissions, and returns bounded tool results. Realtime uses the same owner-fenced authority for native and external tool calls.

components.name: Swift chat coordinator
components.summary: Builds the selected context request, owns visible streaming state, and asks the runtime bridge to execute a query while preserving cancellation and terminal output semantics.

components.name: Swift Node JSONL bridge
components.summary: AgentRuntimeProcess launches the local Node runtime through its bridgePath as a subprocess with JSONL stdio; the Node runtime then launches Pi separately in --mode rpc. Swift frames authenticated wire envelopes and handles query, journal, catalog, context, tool, and cancellation replies.

components.name: Node runtime kernel
components.summary: index.ts admits owner-scoped requests, manages runtime state and pending tool calls, routes kernel operations to local stores, and returns terminal or cancelled outcomes over the Swift protocol.

components.name: Pi model subprocess
components.summary: pi-mono.ts starts the bundled Pi executable as an actual --mode rpc subprocess with JSONL stdio, injects the managed context file and extension pipe, translates model events into runtime projections, and resumes the model after tool results.

components.name: Pi typed tool extension
components.summary: The Pi extension advertises the typed manifest and relays proposals through a private bridge pipe to Swift, waits for a matching result, and returns the result content to Pi with cancellation and timeout handling.

components.name: Selected kernel context
components.summary: ChatProvider.prepareKernelQueryContext resolves the owner session, obtains the kernel snapshot, and assembles identity, memories, goals, tasks, profile, schema, screen, and surface inputs; model-time semantic search remains an authorized tool operation.

components.name: Live session lifecycle
components.summary: RealtimeHubController mints a one-use token through the authenticated backend, prepares voice context, starts the direct Gemini Live session, admits only current owner/turn events, and reconnects or enters bounded batch recovery on failure.

components.name: Live tool and turn journal
components.summary: Realtime callbacks execute owner-fenced native or external tools, send results only while the reducer owns the effect, wait for at most one continuation, and persist the completed or interrupted logical turn to the local journal.

components.name: Voice output and recovery
components.summary: Realtime voice drains local PCM playback and reports usage; provider or hardware failure preserves text and uses the established batch STT, Chat, and OpenAI TTS recovery lane without duplicating already played audio.

components.name: Gemini Live provider
components.summary: External Gemini Live provider owns the direct WebSocket session reached by Swift after the backend mints an ephemeral token; it is distinct from the authenticated backend gateway.

components.name: Gateway request admission
components.summary: The managed chat route validates the native request, rejects client provider keys, applies model and payload bounds, and enforces the authenticated user chat quota before provider execution.

components.name: Chat provider streaming
components.summary: The native Chat backend constructs the server-authenticated Gemini streaming request, observes returned events/usage, and handles cancellation/provider failures. The non-streaming background/embedding proxy is a separate route.

components.name: Gateway response stream
components.summary: The authenticated route exposes provider output as text/event-stream, emits bounded keep-alive and sanitized terminal errors, and returns metered response events to the local Pi runtime.

components.name: Live token service
components.summary: The authenticated realtime route validates provider configuration, posts server-held credentials to Gemini auth_tokens, classifies mint failures, and returns the ephemeral token and expiry to the Swift session.

components.name: Tool authorization admission
components.summary: ChatToolExecutor pins expected owner and authorization state before dispatch, and fail-closes when the owner changes.

components.name: Tool operation dispatch
components.summary: The unchecked dispatcher selects the canonical local operation, permission flow, capture path, retrieval path, or task/memory/conversation handler.

components.name: Local read and mutation operations
components.summary: Authorized operations read semantic/local data and perform SQL reads or writes with owner checks and post-commit refresh effects.

components.name: Tool result owner fence
components.summary: Execution results are checked again against the expected owner and converted to an explicit owner-changed failure before returning to the runtime relay.

components.name: Interface
components.summary: OMIApp hosts the main DesktopHomeView window. DesktopNavigationPolicy resolves stable Home, Memory, Tasks, Insights, Rewind, Settings, and Permissions destinations, while PageContentView renders the corresponding SwiftUI pages; Chat is an effect that opens the Home stage.

components.name: Account & permissions
components.summary: AppState checks and presents macOS permissions. AuthService validates and refreshes Firebase credentials against the persisted owner. RuntimeOwnerIdentity serializes owner transitions, quiesces producers, invalidates prior generations, retargets local stores, and publishes the new owner only after cleanup.

components.name: Local archive
components.summary: The local archive coordinates owner-scoped Swift GRDB and file backed product state: conversations plus Rewind screenshot/OCR/search metadata, embeddings, and local image/video bytes. Owner transitions recover or fence active writers before clearing storage and caches; local account deletion/sign-out is coordinated separately from remote account deletion.

components.name: Swift GRDB and file store
components.summary: The shared Swift store boundary uses the RewindDatabase GRDB pool and RewindStorage per-user files for owner-local product state, including Rewind and other Swift-owned conversation, memory, task and transcript authorities. Owner-authorized APIs check snapshots around reads, writes, and deletion of database rows plus associated files.

components.name: Node local agent SQLite store
components.summary: The local Node agent database heyintentive-agent.sqlite3 owns owner-scoped sessions, runs, attempts, catalog, journal revisions, context, artifacts, and attachment references. Journal insertion, updates, terminalization, replay, and surface wakeups enforce owner and producing-run identity.

components.name: interface page and settings controls
components.summary: The shell sends capture, Chat, Rewind, export, and account actions to the owning local or authenticated service boundaries.

components.name: macOS permission recovery surface
components.summary: Permission state is checked on page appearance and app activation; recovery distinguishes TCC permission from engine failure and opens the relevant System Settings flow.

components.name: effective owner transition fence
components.summary: Owner A work is revoked and producers quiesced before local stores are retargeted to owner B; snapshots prevent delayed reads or mutations from crossing the transition.

components.name: Firebase credential and request boundary
components.summary: Stored and refreshed Firebase tokens are checked against the current owner and session attempt; API request policy also rejects mismatched owner snapshots before network I/O.

components.name: local export and account deletion controls
components.summary: Settings exports owner-local data through a local JSON writer and sends authenticated account deletion to the backend, then stops local producers and signs out through the owner transition.

components.name: Swift Chat draft and attachment bridge
components.summary: ChatProvider persists owner-keyed drafts and staged attachments, materializes bytes in LocalChatAttachmentStore, and sends attachment metadata and managed URIs to the local AgentBridge.

components.name: remote account deletion worker
components.summary: The Firebase-authenticated backend persists deletion intent and dispatches a durable wipe. The worker cancels billing, deletes Firebase Auth, wipes Firestore user data, and reports retry or terminal outcomes without replacing local product authorities.

components.name: Managed Gemini proxy
components.summary: Remote authenticated non-streaming compute proxy for background generation and text embeddings. Participant/paywall checks, model/action allowlist, request bounds and burst/daily limits precede the server-key provider request. Returns provider bytes/status; it does not own local product records.

components.name: Memory candidate compute
components.summary: Remote stateless extract, normalize and consolidate routes require participant authentication and per-operation rate limits. Managed Gemini output is parsed and grounded/validated into bounded proposals; the Mac owns durable jobs, revision checks and record mutation.

components.name: Conversation candidate compute
components.summary: Remote authenticated discard, structure and action-item computation accepts a bounded transcript packet and returns generation-tagged candidates. Errors propagate to local retry/fallback; these routes do not finalize or store the local conversation.

components.name: Gemini model service
components.summary: External Google Gemini generation and embedding APIs. Repository code shows the remote calls and parsing; provider internals and live execution are outside this map. Backend credentials authorize requests; local product storage remains separately owned.

components.name: Simple goals
components.summary: Owner-local GoalStorage authority for active and completed simple goals; profile generation reads active goal titles from this store.

components.name: AI user profile
components.summary: Mac-local AI profile authority that assembles bounded Memory, task/goal, conversation, and Chat journal context, requests a factual two-stage Gemini profile, and stores owner-authorized profile history for local consumers.

components.name: Profile input assembly
components.summary: Loads bounded owner-local memories, action items, active goals, completed conversations from the last seven days, and the recent local Chat journal; failed individual loaders contribute an empty section.

components.name: Profile generation
components.summary: Admits one generation at a time, rejects empty input, builds the factual prompt for the current bounded inputs, and performs the owner-fenced initial profile synthesis.

components.name: Profile consolidation
components.summary: Reads the newly synthesized profile plus up to five prior local profiles, asks Gemini to reconcile current and historical facts, and bounds the consolidated text before local persistence.

components.name: Profile history store
components.summary: Uses the shared owner-local GRDB database to read the newest or bounded history and to insert, edit, delete, or clear profile records, fencing reads and writes with authorization and database generation.

components.name: Local Memory lifecycle worker
components.summary: A local actor cadence loop recovers durable work, leases bounded batches, calls stateless normalize/extract/consolidate compute or embedding compute, validates returned identity and grounding, retries failed work with bounded backoff, and commits only through MemoryStorage owner/revision fences.

components.name: Memory work claim and retry
components.summary: The runner recovers unfinished rows, claims due work under owner generation and retries failures with bounded backoff before terminal state.

components.name: Memory normalization
components.summary: Leased manual or corrected assertions are sent to normalize compute and accepted only with matching request ID and input revision.

components.name: Conversation memory extraction
components.summary: A leased conversation packet is bounded to 500 segments and one content generation; returned candidates must quote exactly one source segment before local admission.

components.name: Memory embedding operation
components.summary: Leased current content is batch embedded through the Gemini proxy and stored only when response count and input revisions align.

components.name: Memory consolidation
components.summary: Leased Short-term candidates receive complete, grounded decisions; promotion, archive, review and rejection are locally fenced, with Long-term targets archived only on valid replacement or merge.

components.name: Screen Memory admission gate
components.summary: Screen analysis requires both the Memory assistant setting and notificationsEnabled; UserDefaults registers notifications disabled by default.

components.name: OCR embedding worker
components.summary: Queues OCR, batches/deduplicates, fences owner generation, requeues ordinary failures, drops expected backend gates and commits local vectors.
